questions.question: What does LLM stand for in the context of AI systems like ChatGPT?
questions.explanation: LLMs are neural networks trained on massive text datasets to generate and understand language.

questions.question: What is generative AI?
options: AI that only classifies existing data
AI that creates new content such as text, images, or audio
AI that translates between programming languages
questions.explanation: Generative AI produces novel content by learning patterns from training data.

questions.question: What is edge computing?
options: Processing data near its source instead of a distant data center
A technique for sharper display rendering
Running all workloads on a single central server
questions.explanation: Edge computing reduces latency and bandwidth by processing data close to where it is generated.

questions.question: What is the basic unit of information in quantum computing?
questions.explanation: A qubit can exist in a superposition of 0 and 1, unlike a classical bit.

questions.question: What does the '5G' in mobile networks refer to?
questions.explanation: 5G is the fifth generation of cellular networks, offering higher speeds and lower latency than 4G.

questions.question: What is blockchain fundamentally?
options: A single encrypted database owned by one company
A distributed, append-only ledger of transactions
A compression algorithm for large files
questions.explanation: Blockchain records transactions in linked blocks replicated across many nodes.

questions.question: What does XR stand for as an umbrella term for immersive technologies?
questions.explanation: XR covers virtual reality, augmented reality, and mixed reality technologies.

questions.question: What does augmented reality do?
options: Completely replaces the real world with a virtual one
Blocks all digital content from view
Overlays digital information onto the real world
questions.explanation: AR adds digital elements like images or labels on top of the user's real-world view.

questions.question: What is a digital twin?
options: A virtual replica of a physical object or system
A backup copy of a hard drive
questions.explanation: Digital twins mirror real-world assets so engineers can simulate and monitor them.

questions.question: What does the zero trust security model assume?
options: No user or device is trusted by default, even inside the network
questions.explanation: Zero trust continuously verifies every request regardless of where it originates.

questions.question: In cloud computing, what does SaaS provide?
options: Complete applications accessed over the internet
A platform for developers to deploy code
questions.explanation: Software as a Service delivers finished applications through a browser on subscription.

questions.question: In cloud computing, what does IaaS provide?
options: Fundamental computing resources like virtual machines and storage
questions.explanation: Infrastructure as a Service rents computing, storage, and networking on demand.

questions.question: What is an AI 'hallucination'?
options: A visual glitch in VR headsets
An AI model confidently generating false or made-up information
When a computer dreams in sleep mode
questions.explanation: Hallucination describes plausible-sounding but incorrect output from language models.

questions.question: What is prompt engineering?
options: Crafting inputs that guide AI models toward desired outputs
questions.explanation: Prompt engineering is the practice of designing effective inputs for AI systems.

questions.question: What is a smart contract?
options: Self-executing code on a blockchain that enforces an agreement
questions.explanation: Smart contracts automatically execute terms when coded conditions are met.

questions.question: What is deep learning?
options: Machine learning using neural networks with many layers
A type of long-term data storage
questions.explanation: Deep learning uses multi-layered neural networks to learn complex patterns from data.

questions.question: In the context of LLMs, what is a token?
options: A chunk of text the model processes, such as part of a word
questions.explanation: LLMs break input into tokens — word pieces or characters — for processing.

questions.question: What is multimodal AI?
options: AI that works on multiple computers
AI that can process several types of input such as text, images, and audio
AI that supports several programming languages
questions.explanation: Multimodal models understand and combine different data types like images and speech.

questions.question: What does retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) do?
options: Supplements an AI model's answers with relevant documents fetched at query time
questions.explanation: RAG grounds model responses in retrieved external information to improve accuracy.

questions.question: What is elasticity in cloud computing?
options: Automatically scaling resources up or down based on demand
questions.explanation: Elasticity lets cloud systems adjust capacity dynamically to match workload.

questions.question: What is superposition in quantum computing?
options: A qubit's ability to represent a combination of 0 and 1 simultaneously
Running two operating systems at once
questions.explanation: Superposition lets qubits encode multiple states at once, enabling parallel exploration.

questions.question: What key advantage does 5G offer over 4G for applications like autonomous vehicles?
options: Much lower latency and higher device density
questions.explanation: 5G reduces response delay to milliseconds and supports far more devices per area.

questions.question: What is mixed reality (MR)?
options: An environment where digital objects interact with the physical world in real time
questions.explanation: MR anchors interactive digital content to the real world, blending AR and VR concepts.

questions.question: What is fine-tuning of an AI model?
options: Further training a pretrained model on a specific dataset
questions.explanation: Fine-tuning adapts a general model to specialized tasks using additional data.

questions.question: What is serverless computing?
options: A model where the cloud provider manages servers and runs code on demand
Running a website from a phone
questions.explanation: Serverless abstracts infrastructure away; providers allocate resources per function call.

questions.question: What is green computing?
options: Designing and using IT in an environmentally sustainable way
questions.explanation: Green computing aims to reduce energy use and electronic waste in IT systems.
